reason: Fusion copies uninitialized heap bytes with account identifiers, home paths and cloud ids into saved archives, so these fixtures were rewritten with same-length placeholders before publication. Protein AssetData property stores are a 16-byte header followed by 136-byte blocks, and each block's 8-byte header records how many of its 128 capacity bytes are used; the truncated-key rule reads only the unused capacity after those bytes, and the bare-value rule accepts a value only when its quote, colon and quote begin exactly where that unused capacity begins. In AssetData members that are not block stores, the truncated-key rule reads the whole member and the bare-value rule is off. The placeholders list holds every placeholder already written, and values inside those placeholders are left unchanged, so a second run makes no replacement.
capturedReason: The reflection capture archive recorded absolute home paths, which were rewritten to repository-relative or home-relative form.
